sources.title: Pagden: Pocock’s political-language model in the Introduction (1987)
sources.citation: Anthony Pagden, “Introduction,” in Pagden, ed., The Languages of Political Theory in Early-Modern Europe (Cambridge University Press, 1987), 1–18. doi: 10.1017/CBO9780511521447.001.

verification.note: Freshly read complete substantive opening excerpt reproduced under Summary on the publisher page; this is actual methodological prose, not publication metadata alone. It explicitly uses Pocock’s language-game formulation. Exact printed page is not asserted; complete introduction and Pocock’s contribution remain unread. sources.title: Pagden: Todorov resource and feedback in Letters from Mexico (2001 witness)
sources.citation: Anthony Pagden, acknowledgments and Introduction, in Hernán Cortés, Letters from Mexico, trans. and ed. Anthony Pagden, with an introductory essay by J. H. Elliott (Yale Nota Bene, 2001; originally 1971, revised edition 1986), vi and lv n. 43.

verification.note: Fresh facsimile reading and visual collation: title/copyright leaves, acknowledgments vi (PDF 11), Pagden Introduction lv (PDF 60), including Todorov note 43. Pagden explicitly uses a particular Todorov interpretation and credits Todorov/Kagan/Delgado as readers offering improvements. Cortés authors the letters; Pagden’s introduction differs from Elliott’s essay. The 2001 edition states original 1971 and revised 1986; exact timing of every introductory revision is not established. No whole-volume or original Todorov-body reading claimed.
